questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Talikota fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccan sultanates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1565 AD.**__

__
 
• Battle of Talikota, confrontation in the Deccan region of southern India between the forces of the **Hindu raja of Vijayanagar and the four allied Muslim sultans of Bijapur, Bidar, Ahmadnagar, and Golconda.**

 
 
• The battle was fought in **January, 1565**, at a site southeast of Bijapur, in what is now northern Karnataka state.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Krishna Deva Raya, king of the Vijaynagar empire at its zenith, stormed the Raichur Fort after a bloodily victorious battle against the forces of Ismail Adil Shah, ruler of the Bijapur Sultanate.
 
 
• The Battle of Raichur (1520), though celebrated widely through the streets of Vijayanagara, signaled the slow-yet-steady downfall of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Ultimately, the Battle of Talikota (1565) brought about the fated decline of a kingdom over two hundred years old.
 
• After this decisive battle, the Vijayanagara Empire could never reach the same heights of the past.

questions.question: Vijay Stambh was built by which of these rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Kumbha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vijay Stambha is an imposing victory monument located in Chittorgarh fort in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan.
 
• It was constructed by Mewar king Rana Kumbha in 1448 to commemorate his victory over the combined armies of Malwa and Gujarat led by Mahmud Khilji.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rana Kumbha (1417-1468)**

 
 
• Reign of Mewar: Rana Kumbha was a powerful ruler of the Mewar kingdom in Rajasthan, India, reigning from 1433 to 1468 CE.
 
• Military Prowess: He was a renowned warrior who expanded the boundaries of Mewar through numerous successful military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms.
 
• Architectural Patronage: Kumbha is celebrated for his significant contributions to architecture. He commissioned the construction of the magnificent Kumbhalgarh Fort, one of the most impregnable fortresses in India. He also patronized the building of numerous Hindu and Jain temples, showcasing intricate stone carvings and sculptures.
 
• Cultural Patronage: Kumbha was a patron of arts and literature. He was himself a skilled musician and a scholar, contributing to the development of Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Durga Das Rathore (1638-1718)**
 
 
• Loyal General: Durga Das Rathore was a renowned Rajput general who served under several Mughal emperors, including Aurangzeb.
 
• Master Strategist: He was known for his military brilliance and strategic acumen.
 
• Champion of Rajput Pride: Despite serving the Mughals, Durga Das remained fiercely loyal to his Rajput heritage and often championed the cause of Rajput independence.
 
• Key Role in Rajput Resistance: He played a crucial role in uniting Rajput clans against Mughal dominance, fostering a sense of collective resistance.
 
 
 
• **Maharana Pratap (1540-1597)**
 
 
• Ruler of Mewar: Maharana Pratap was a valiant ruler of Mewar who famously resisted Mughal emperor Akbar's attempts to conquer his kingdom.
 
• Symbol of Rajput Resistance: He is a revered figure in Indian history, symbolizing Rajput valor and resistance against foreign rule.
 
• The Battle of Haldighati: The Battle of Haldighati, fought between Pratap and Akbar's forces, is legendary. Though the outcome was inconclusive, Pratap's courage and resilience in the face of overwhelming odds have earned him legendary status.
 
• Guerrilla Warfare: After the Battle of Haldighati, Pratap resorted to guerrilla warfare tactics to continue his resistance against the Mughals, effectively keeping them out of Mewar for much of his reign.
 
 
 
• **Prithvi Raj Chauhan (c. 1178-1192)**
 
 
• Last Hindu Shahi Ruler of Delhi and Ajmer: Prithvi Raj Chauhan was the last Hindu Shahi ruler of Delhi and Ajmer.
 
• Conquest of Delhi: He succeeded in capturing Delhi from the Ghaznavids, restoring Hindu rule to the region.
 
• Conflict with Muhammad Ghori: He engaged in a series of battles with the Afghan ruler Muhammad Ghori.

questions.question: The famous tripartite struggle was fought for control over ________ in early medieval period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannauj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tripartite Struggle,** commonly referred to as the **Kannauj Triangle Wars,** transpired in the ninth century, revolving around the **battle for dominance in northern India** among three prominent empires**: the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire, the Pala Empire, and the Rashtrakuta Empire.**
 
• This intense conflict primarily revolved around asserting control over the city of Kannauj, which served as a pivotal symbol of authority over the Ganges plain.
 
• During this period, the** Palas of Bengal, the Pratiharas of Central India, and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan** engaged in fierce warfare to secure their influence over Kannauj.
 
• Ultimately, the Pratiharas emerged as the triumphant force, consolidating their power and dominance in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kannauj, **located in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, serves as both a city and an administrative center, functioning as a municipal board or Nagar Palika Parishad within Kannauj district. The name "Kannauj" is an evolved form of the classical name "Kanyakubja".
 
• Historically, it was also known as "Mahodaya" during the reign of Mihira Bhoja. Positioned 104 kilometers west of the state capital, Lucknow, Kannauj has been a significant center throughout Classical India, serving as a focal point for various imperial Indian dynasties.
 
• Among these dynasties, the earliest was the Maukhari dynasty, followed by Emperor Harsha of the Vardhana dynasty. Subsequently, Kannauj came under the rule of the Gahadavala dynasty, attaining unprecedented glory under the reign of Govindachandra.

questions.question: In which year was Battle of Peshawar fought between Raja Jayapal and Mahmud Ghazni?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Battle of Peshawar between Raja Jayapala **and **Mahmud of Ghazni **took place in the year **1001 CE.**
 
• **Raja Jayapala **was the ruler of the **Hindu Shahi dynasty** in the region, while **Mahmud of Ghazni** was a prominent **Muslim conqueror** from the Ghaznavid dynasty.
 
• The battle resulted in the defeat of **Raja Jayapala** and marked the beginning of **Mahmud's invasions** into the **Indian subcontinent.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Hindu Shahi dynasty** was a** medieval Indian dynasty** that ruled the region of **Gandhara (present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan)** from the **9th to the 10th centuries CE.**
 
• They were known as the** "Shahi" **or** "Kings of the Shahis"** and were primarily of **Hindu faith,** although some rulers may have embraced **Buddhism **as well.
 
• The dynasty's origins are believed to be in the **ancient Gandhara region,** which had a rich history and was a center of Buddhist culture.
 
• The Hindu Shahis emerged as a powerful dynasty in the wake of the decline of the** Turk Shahi dynasty.**
 
• **The Hindu Shahi rulers** were known for their resistance against the **Arab and Turkic invasions** from the west.
 
• They successfully defended their territories against several attempts at conquest by Muslim armies, including the expeditions of Arab general Qutayba ibn Muslim in the 8th century.

questions.question: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was constructed in around 1197 AD by the sultan of which of the following dynasties of Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mamluk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mamluk:**
 
• The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was commissioned by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Mamluk dynasty (also known as the Slave dynasty).
 
• Construction began around 1193 AD and was completed in approximately 1197 AD.
 
• The mosque was built using the remains of demolished Hindu and Jain temples, reflecting the early Islamic conquests in India.
 
• It is considered one of the earliest existing mosques in India.
 
• The Mamluk dynasty was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lodhi:**
 
• The Lodhi dynasty was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1451 to 1526 AD.
 
• They were known for their architectural contributions, primarily tombs and gardens.
 
• They came to power much later than the construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.
 
• The Lodhi dynasty was defeated by Babur.
 
• Their architecture style was very different from the early sultanate.
 
• **Tughlaq:**
 
• The Tughlaq dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320 to 1414 AD.
 
• They were known for their ambitious projects, including the construction of forts and irrigation systems.
 
• While they were a significant dynasty, their rule came after the initial establishment of the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.
 
• They were known for building strong fortifications.
 
• They ruled during a time of expansion, and then decline of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• **Khalji:**
 
• The Khalji dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1290 to 1320 AD.
 
• They were known for their military conquests and administrative reforms.
 
• Although they expanded the Delhi Sultanate, they came to power after the Mamluks and the initial construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.
 
• Alauddin Khalji was a very powerful ruler of this dynasty.
 
• They were known for their agressive military campaigns.

questions.question: Raichur doab, the land between Krishna and Tungabhadra was a region of conflict between the kings of Vijayanagar and ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahamani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raichur doab**, the land between **Krishna and Tungabhadra **was a reason for conflict between **the kings of Vijayanagar and Bahamani.**
 
• **The Raichur-Tungabhadra Doab region** was a frequent battleground between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms.
 
• Situated in the southern Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, the Raichur Doab is a triangular landmass between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers.
 
• Both kingdoms sought control over this region due to its wealth and economic resources.
 
• With ambitious and formidable rulers, they aimed to annex and assert dominance over each other's territories.
 
• Religious differences further fueled the conflict, as the majority of the southern population adhered to Hinduism, while the northern populace followed Islam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Malwa** is a historical region situated in west-central India, encompassing a plateau of volcanic origin.
 
• **Golconda** is a fortified citadel and abandoned city situated in the western outskirts of Hyderabad, Telangana, India.
 
• **The Bengal Sultanate** was a late medieval sultanate established in the Bengal region during the 14th to 16th century.

questions.question: Whose descendants were the Mughals from their father’s side?
questions.solution: Two great lineages of rulers were the ancestors of the Mughals. From their maternal side they were the descendants of Genghis Khan (who died in 1227) who ruled the Mongol tribes, China and Central Asia. From their paternal side they were the descendants of Timur who ruled Iraq, Iran and modern-day Turkey. Timur died in the year 1404. Babar (1526 – 1530) was the first Mughal emperor.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a type of sacrifice performed by kings in ancient India to establish their position?
questions.solution:
__**Muvendavelan**__ was **NOT **a type of sacrifice performed by **kings in ancient India to establish their position.**

 
• **Muvendavelan** was a famous military officer of the Chola Empire, known for his generous donation to the numerous temples where he had been deployed by the king.
 
• **The Rajasuya** is connected with the consecration of the King and is prescribed as a way of maintaining the king's sovereignty.
 
• It involves a game of throwing dice, in which the king is enthroned and the world is regenerated.
 
• **Vajapeya Yagna** has been performed to preserve peace in the state. It's the highest form of Soma Yajna.
 
• **Ashvamedha Yagna** was performed by the King for fertility and strength in the kingdom.
 
• It is a rite of horse sacrifice accompanied by the** practice of the Vedic religion of the Shrauta.** This has been used by ancient Indian kings to assert their colonial supremacy.

questions.question: This temple, that was built by Raja Bhimdev I of the Solanki Dynasty, has a rectangular pond called ‘Surya Kund’ in front of it. What is the name of this temple?

The correct answer is __**Modhera Sun Temple**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The temple is located in **Modhera, Gujarat, India.**
 
• The temple is **dedicated to the Hindu sun god, Lord Surya**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Khajuraho****​**

 
 
• The Khajuraho Group of Monuments is a group of Hindu temples and Jain temples lo in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh.
 
• They are a World Heritage site by UNESCO. The temples are famous for their architectural symbolism of the nagara-style and their erotic sculptures.
 
• Most Khajuraho temples were constructed by the Chandela dynasty between 950 AD and 1050 AD.
 
• Historical records mention that by the 12th century, the temple site of Khajuraho had 85 temples, spread over 20 square kilometres.
 
• A profusion of sculptures from the surviving temples with intricate details, symbolism and expressiveness of ancient Indian art adorns the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple.
 
 
 
• **Konark Sun Templ**e
 
 
• Konark Sun Temple was built in 1250 AD.
 
 
• This temple is also called "Black Pagoda".
 
• Temple was declared World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1984.
 
• Famous Chandrabhaga Mela took place here every year in the month of February.
 
• This temple is attributed to King Narsimhadeva - I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty.
 
• Temple is a classic illustration of Great Kalinga Architecture.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Chausath Yogini****​**
 
 
• Chausath Yogini Temple is devoted to Goddess Durga and the 64 Yoginis who are observed to be her different forms, the Chausath Yogini Temple is constructed with local granite. 
 
• The statues of the Yoginis have been arranged circularly and have been carved intricately.
 
• The Chausath Yogini Temple, Morena, also popular as Ekattarso Mahadeva Temple, Stands atop an isolated hill approximately a hundred feet high, this circular temple commands a splendid view of the cultivated fields below. 
 
• This temple is so famous due to the presence of a multitude of Shivalingas inside its cells.

questions.question: Who among the following kings founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishnadevaraya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krishnadevaraya:**

 
 
• Krishnadevaraya, the ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded the suburban township of **Nagalapuram** near Vijayanagara.
 
• He named the town after his mother, Nagala Devi, as a tribute to her.
 
• Krishnadevaraya was one of the greatest rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire, reigning from 1509 to 1529.
 
• He was a patron of art, literature, and architecture, and his reign is considered the golden age of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Nagalapuram was developed as a cultural and administrative center during his rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deva Raya II:**

 
 
• Deva Raya II was a prominent ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire who reigned from 1424 to 1446.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and administrative reforms.
 
• However, he is not associated with the founding of Nagalapuram.
 
• His reign is marked by the expansion of the empire and patronage of literature and arts.
 
• He is often referred to as one of the most powerful rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
 
 
• **Rajaraja Chola:**
 
 
• Rajaraja Chola I was a great Chola emperor who ruled from 985 to 1014 CE.
 
• He is renowned for his military conquests, architectural achievements, and the construction of the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur.
 
• His reign marked the peak of the Chola Empire's power and influence.
 
• However, he belonged to the Chola dynasty and is not connected to the Vijayanagara Empire or Nagalapuram.
 
• His contributions were primarily in South India, particularly in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra I:**
 
 
• Rajendra Chola I, the son of Rajaraja Chola, ruled from 1014 to 1044 CE.
 
• He expanded the Chola Empire to its greatest extent, including parts of Southeast Asia.
 
• He is known for his naval expeditions and the construction of the city of Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
 
• Like Rajaraja Chola, he belonged to the Chola dynasty and is unrelated to the Vijayanagara Empire or Nagalapuram.
 
• His reign is celebrated for its military and cultural achievements.

questions.question: The Battle of Karnal is known for the invasion of which of the following aggressors against India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nadir Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Karnal** occurred in **1739**, when **Nadir Shah**, the ruler of the Afsharid dynasty of Persia, invaded India.
 
• He** defeated the Mughal army** **led **by **Muhammad Shah** at Karnal and subsequently sacked Delhi, the Mughal capital.
 
• This decisive victory marked the beginning of the decline of the Mughal Empire.
 
• **Afsharid Dynasty**:
 
 
• The **Turkoman Afshar tribe** in **Iran's northeastern area of Khorasan** gave rise to the Afsharid dynasty, which **controlled Iran (Persia) in the middle of the eighteenth century**.
 
• **Nadir Shah (Nader Shah Afshar)**, a brilliant military tactician who deposed the final Safavid dynasty member and crowned himself Shah of Iran, **founded **the **dynasty **in **1736**.
 
• Under Nader's leadership, Iran reached its widest point since the Sasanian Empire.
 
• At its height, it **controlled **portions of **Iraq**, **Turkey**, the **United Arab Emirates**, and **Oman **in addition to modern-day **Iran**, **Armenia**, **Georgia**, the **Azerbaijan **Republic, **Afghanistan**, **Bahrain**, **Turkmenistan**, **Uzbekistan**, and **Pakistan**, as well as portions of the **North Caucasus (Dagestan)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ahmed Shah Abdali**:

 
 
• The **founder of the Durrani Empire** and the modern state of Afghanistan was Ahmad Shah Abdali, sometimes referred to as Ahmad Khan Abdali or **Ahmad Shah Durrani**.
 
• **After Nadir Shah passed away in 1747**, **Abdali **was selected to** take over **and attacked India on several occasions between 1748 and 1767.
 
• During this period, he **launched eight invasions of India**, conquered Punjab, and **defeated the Marathas** in the **Third Battle of Panipat in 1761**.
 
 
 
• **Shah Shuja**:
 
 
• The **second child** of Mughal Emperor **Shah Jahan** and Empress **Mumtaz Mahal **was Mirza Shah Shuja.
 
• He served as **governor** of both **Bengal **and **Odisha**; his **capital **was **Dhaka**.
 
• Following Shah Jahan's sickness in September of 1657, the brothers had a power struggle.
 
• **Shah Shuja** declared himself to be the Emperor, but **Aurangzeb **took the Dehli throne and dispatched Mir Jumla to bring Shuja under control.
 
• On January 5, **1659**, **Shuja lost** the** Battle of Khajwa**.
 
 
 
• **Nasir Khan**:
 
 
• While Nasir Khan **participated in rebellions against the Mughal Empire**, he wasn't involved in the Battle of Karnal.

questions.question: In medieval architecture, Sarais are places used for _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**temporary accommodation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sarais were essentially inns or rest houses established in medieval times.
 
• They provided temporary accommodation for travelers, merchants, and pilgrims.
 
• These structures were often found along trade routes and were crucial for the safety and comfort of travelers.
 
• Sarais typically included facilities like rooms for sleeping, stables for animals, and sometimes even food provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medieval Architecture**

 
 
• Medieval architecture refers to the architectural styles that were prevalent in Europe during the Middle Ages, roughly from the 5th to the late 15th century.
 
• It includes a variety of styles such as Romanesque, Gothic, and Byzantine.
 
• Key features of medieval architecture include the use of stone, pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses.
 
• Buildings from this period include castles, churches, and fortifications, all serving different purposes from defense to religious worship.
 
 
 
• **Trade Routes**
 
 
• Trade routes were essential pathways used for the commercial movement of goods and services.
 
• They facilitated the exchange of commodities like spices, silk, precious metals, and other goods between different regions.
 
• Famous medieval trade routes include the Silk Road, the Amber Road, and the Trans-Saharan trade routes.
 
• These routes not only boosted economic activity but also enabled cultural and technological exchanges between civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Hospices and Inns**
 
 
• Similar to sarais, hospices and inns were established to offer lodging and care for travelers and pilgrims.
 
• Hospices, often run by religious institutions, provided free or low-cost shelter and food to the needy and the sick.
 
• Inns were more commercial establishments that charged for lodging and meals, catering mainly to merchants and other travelers.
 
• These facilities played a significant role in medieval society by promoting travel and commerce.

questions.question: The policy of Permanent Settlement was introduced in India in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1793**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Permanent Settlement, also known as the Zamindari System__, was introduced in Bengal by the East India Company under Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
 
• The system was designed as a legal regime to stabilize property ownership and encourage the landowning Zamindars to improve the agricultural productivity of the lands they governed over.
 
• Its key feature was the fixing of tax obligations in perpetuity.
 
• The taxation rights were given to Zamindars, who were expected to collect these taxes from the peasant communities that resided on the land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Permanent Settlement was first introduced in Bengal and Bihar and later expanded to Varanasi and the south district of Madras.
 
• It eventually spread all over northern India courtesy of a series of regulations promulgated on 1st May 1793.
 
• These regulations persisted until the Charter Act of 1833 came to hold.
 
• The Permanent Settlement marked a significant chapter in the economic and social history of colonial India, shaping the contours of social power and land relations in regions it was introduced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.britannica.com/76/130376-050-CDB90B38/Charles-Cornwallis-1st-Marquess.jpg]

questions.question: Dharmasutras contain ______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**norms for rulers.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• There are many diverse and **opposing Dharmashastras,** with estimates ranging from **18 to about 100.**
 
• The Dharmasastra textual corpus, which was written in **poetic verses**, is a part of the **Hindu Smritis.**
 
• It contains several commentaries and treatises on one's obligations to** one's self, one's family, and society.**

questions.question: Indra Sawhney and others vs UOI case is related to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reservation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8eb9bb679eedf2fb873b59b31494e3eadcbcae26fe76a1ea53721b18ee81afd.png] 

**Indra Sawhney v. Union of India 1992:**

 
• At the beginning of the 1990s, the central government **implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations** for reservation of other backward classes.
 
• This created chaos in various sections of the society.
 
• Consequently, a PIL was filed, and resulted in one of the most significant judgments namely “**Indra Sawhney case”. **
 
• Also known as Mandal Case.
 
• Became **the cornerstone in the present reservation structure of the country. So, option 2 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6a8f06b262806456af665e1b8217ceb8113d6bb49456f9395913c6248cabbdd.png] 

**Salient features of Indra Sawhney judgment:**

 
• It **recognized socially and economically backward classes** as a category and recognized the** validity of the 27 percent reservation**.
 
• The **concept of the ‘creamy layer’ gained currency** through this judgment.
 
• Those among the OBCs who had transcended their social backwardness were to be excluded from the reservation.
 
• It laid down **a 50 percent limit on reservations** and observed that economic, social, and educational criteria were needed to define backward classes.
 
• **Reservation for backward classes** (which include OBCs and SCs & STs) should be **confined to initial appointments and not extend to promotions.**

questions.question: What was the revenue system during Mughal emperor Akbar’s reign called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zabt System.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The revenue system during Akbar’s reign was called **Zabt System.**
 
• **Raja Todar Mal **was** Akbar's finance minister,** he introduced this system.
 
• He took a careful survey of crop yields and prices cultivated for a **10 years** period **1570-1580.**
 
• The system of taxation was called **Dahshala.**
 
• In this system, each province was divided into revenue circles with their own rates of revenue for each crop.
 
• On this basis, the tax was fixed on each **crop in cash.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Akbar was one of the mightiest emperors during the Mughal Era.
 
• He was born in October 1542 and died on 27th October 1605.
 
• Akbar was the third Mughal Emperor.
 
• His reign was between 1556-1605 AD.
 
• He was crowned in 1556, at the young age of thirteen years.
 
• He was assisted by Barram Khan.
 
• He is known for his liberal religious policies, relationship with Indian kings, conquests, etc.
 
• In 1564, he abolished the jizyah tax levied on non-muslims.
 
• Akbar introduced Mansabdari System in his administration.

questions.question: When was the Battle of Tukaroi fought where Akbar defeated Sultanate of Bengal and Bihar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1575.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The Battle of Tukaroi **was fought on **March 3, 1575,** between the Mughal Empire led by** Akbar and** the Sultanate of Bengal and Bihar led by** Daud Khan Karrani.**
 
• It was a significant battle in the history of medieval India, as it marked the beginning of the end of the** Karrani dynasty's rule in Bengal and Bihar.**
 
• Akbar's victory in the Battle of Tukaroi was due to his **superior military tactics and the effective use of firearms**, which gave the Mughals an edge over their opponents.
 
• **The battle was also significant because it paved the way for Akbar's expansion **of the Mughal Empire in the east, eventually leading to the annexation of Bengal and Bihar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information __****Source: https://ignca.gov.in/Asi_data/74742.pdf (Page No- 12)**
